15076.name: Bent-over W-shape Stretch
15076.description: bend your knees and bend down, keep your body at an angle of 30° to 45° to the ground, bend your elbows, and clench your fists with thumbs outward. extend your arms to a w-shape with your body, relax your shoulders, clench your elbows, and feel the muscles of your mid-back and the middle of your back being squeezed. straighten your back, and keep your head in a straight line with your spine.
15076.breathing: exhale when stretching, and inhale when restoring.
15076.key_points: when the force is released, the middle back has a distinct squeezing sensation.
15076.mistakes:
mistake: did not take the shoulder as the axis when tightening the back backward, and spread out your elbows.

mistake: bend and arch your back.
solution: tighten the core of the waist and abdominal muscles, and keep your back straight.
15076.notes:
clamp the elbows inward.

15142.name: Bare-handed Cuban Press
15142.description: stand naturally, keep your chest out and stomach in, and place your fists in the front of your thighs. lift your arms until your big arms are parallel to the ground, keep your small arms at a 90-degree angle to your big arms and a 45-degree angle to the ground, with your fists down. using the upper arm as the axis, rotate the small arm upward until it is perpendicular to the ground. push up the arm with your fist forward and bring your arms closer to the middle. lower your big arm until it is parallel to the ground, and the small arm is at a 90-degree angle to the big arm. using the big arm as the axis, rotate the small arm downward to a 45-degree angle with the ground. lower your arms to the front of your thighs.
15142.breathing: exhale when you raise your arms and inhale when you lower your arms.
15142.key_points: there is a clear sense of contraction in the middle and back of the shoulder and in the area between the big arm and the back, but there is no sense of strong force.
15142.mistakes:
mistake: too fast.
solution: pause slightly after each stage of the action.
15142.notes:
lift the elbow and keep the big arm parallel to the ground.
do not shrug your shoulders.

15154.name: Dumbbell Curls
15154.description: stand naturally, keep your chest up and contract your abdominal muscles. clench your hips, keep your body stable, and keep your shoulders back and down, away from your ears. hold the dumbbells in both hands with the palms facing forward, and keep the big arms close to the body and fixed. with the front of the big arms forces, bend the arms and lift the dumbbells until they are close to the chest, pause briefly, and squeeze the arms. slowly unload the force and return to the starting position, and do not fully relax at the lowest point and do not fully straighten the arms. keep the arms fixed and close to the body during the movement.
15154.breathing: exhale when bending, and inhale when falling.
15154.key_points:
when bending, there is a clear sense of contraction on the front side of the big arm.
when falling to the lowest point, the whole arm feels tight.
15154.mistakes:
mistake: when bending, the body swings back and forth to borrow strength, resulting in poor training effect and discomfort in the waist.
solution: control the movement speed, maintain muscle control, do not swing the dumbbells, tighten your hips and abdomen, stabilize the body, and reduce the weight of the dumbbells if the weight is too heavy.
mistake: shrug your shoulders, and swing your body up and down
solution: always keep your chest up and your shoulders away from your ears as much as possible.
15154.notes:
keep your chest up and shoulders down, and keep your shoulder blades and shoulder joints stable and still.
keep your big arms close to your body and fixed.
tighten the abdomen and keep the core stable.
do not completely relax at the lowest point, and do not fully straighten your arms.

15160.name: Alternate Dumbbell Curls
15160.description: keep your feet together, tighten your abdominal muscles, and sink your shoulders. hold the dumbbells in both hands on both sides of your body with your fists facing each other. the force is mainly generated by the elbow joint. bend one arm to lift the dumbbell until it is close to the chest while rotating the arm to bring the fist upward; pause for a moment. during the movement, keep your eyes on the front of the big arm on that side. slowly unload the force and return to the starting position, do not fully relax at the lowest point and do not fully straighten the arm; pause briefly to do the other side of the lift.
15160.breathing: exhale when bending, and inhale when falling.
15160.key_points:

when falling to the lowest point, the whole arm feels tight.
15160.mistakes:
mistake: when bending, the body swings back and forth to borrow strength, resulting in poor training effect and discomfort in the waist.
solution: reduce the weight of the dumbbells; or bend forward slightly.
15160.notes:
tighten the waist and abdominal muscles to keep the body stable.
keep your chest up and sink your shoulders.

15166.name: Right-side Kettlebell Bent-over Row
15166.description: support your left hand on your left knee, the left foot steps on the ground in a diagonal backward direction, and keep your back straight. lead your right shoulder forward, hold the dumbbell, and keep your arms perpendicular to the ground. use your back to force and pull your big arms backward and upward against the body until the elbows are slightly above the torso, and stop briefly at the highest point. unload the force slowly, restore to the starting position, and do not fully relax at the lowest point.
15166.breathing: inhale when lowering, and exhale when pulling up.
15166.key_points:
when pulling up, the back has a distinct sense of contraction, and at the highest point, there is a certain sense of squeezing.
when falling to the lowest point, the back feels slightly pulled.
15166.mistakes:
mistake: at the lowest point, the shoulder is not pulled forward, resulting in inadequate force on the back when pulling up.
solution: at the lowest point, lean your shoulder forward to open the scapula.

15178.name: Right-side Bent-over Tricep Extension With Resistance Band
15178.description: stand with your feet apart and step on the resistance band, bend your hips and stoop about 70°. hold the left arm on the knee to stabilize the body, and clamp the body with the right arm to pull the resistance band. make sure only the right small arm is in motion all over the body, and tense your arm for 1 second when it is straight.
15178.breathing: exhale when the arm is straightened and inhale when restored.
15178.key_points:
there is a distinct sense of contraction at the back of the upper arm when the force is applied.
keep the erector spine muscle and the back of the shoulder tight throughout.
15178.mistakes:
mistake: swing your body to borrow strength, bend, and stoop.
solution: tighten the waist and abdominal muscles throughout the process, straighten your back and slow down the movement.

15184.name: Bent-over Dumbbell Tricep Extension
15184.description: stand naturally, bend your knees slightly, try to bend over until your back is parallel to the ground, and tighten your waist and abdominal muscles. hold the dumbbells with both hands, and clamp the big arms against both sides of the body. straighten your arms, pause briefly and bend your elbows until your small arms are perpendicular to the ground.
15184.breathing: exhale when you straighten your arm and inhale when you bend your elbow and put down the dumbbell.
15184.key_points:
keep your lower back tense throughout the movement.
when you straighten your arm, you will feel a distinct contraction on the back of your big arm; you may feel a slight burning sensation after many times.
15184.mistakes:
mistake: arch your back, and swing your big arms up and down.
solution: reduce the bending range, keep the whole back straight; clamp your big arms simultaneously, keep them close to the sides of the body throughout.
15184.notes:
bend down, tighten your waist and abdominal muscles, and keep your back straight.
straighten your elbows and clamp the body with big arms.
bend your knees.

15190.name: Nod And Raise Head
15190.description: sit on the chair, put your hands on the thighs naturally, keep the waist and back straight, and keep your back close to the chair. put your hands behind the cervical spine to ensure the neck is fixed throughout the movement. when nodding your head, keep your lower jaw close to your neck, and when raising your head, raise your lower jaw upward.
15190.key_points:
when nodding your head, the muscles at the back of the neck feel slightly pulled.
when raising your head, the front muscles of the neck feel slightly pulled.
after the movement, there is a sense of stretching in the neck.
15190.mistakes:
mistake: your neck swings back and forth, following your head nodding and raising.
solution: hold the back side of the cervical spine with your hand and slowly complete the movement while keeping the cervical spine still.
15190.notes:
keep your neck fixed throughout the whole movement.
keep your head down and chin close to the neck.

15196.name: Two-way Head Turn
15196.description: sit in a chair, put your hands naturally on your thighs, and keep your waist straight and your back close to the chair. turn your head to one side, stay for a while, then turn back, and then turn to the other side. try your best to look behind when you turn your head, which will increase the pulling sensation of the neck.

15202.name: Shrug And Sink The Shoulders
15202.description: stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, keep your chest up, stomach in, and shoulders down, and put your arms naturally on both sides of the body. raise your shoulder blades to the maximum extent, with a slight pause; then sink your shoulder blades to the maximum extent, with a slight pause; repeat the process in turn.

15220.name: Half Roll Back
15220.description: sit on the yoga mat, keep your legs slightly bent and hip-width apart, and keep your back straight. when inhaling, extend your head and spine towards the ceiling. when exhaling, roll your tailbone toward the pubis, tighten the pelvic floor muscles, tilt the pelvis backward, and slowly flex the spine backward. make your spine form a "c" with a sense of extension. inhale and return to the starting position.
15220.breathing:
inhale through the nose.
exhale through the mouth.
15220.key_points: tighten your pelvic floor muscles and abdominal muscles.
15220.mistakes:
mistake: your waist bulges back excessively.
solution: lean back your pelvis slightly and drive your spine as a whole to extend backward.
15220.notes:
exhale, roll the tailbone toward the pubis, tilt the pelvis backward and tighten the abdominal muscles.
keep your spine extended.

15226.name: Kneeling Right-side Torso Twist
15226.description: lie prone on a yoga mat with your knees on the ground and slightly apart; put your left hand on the ground and bend your right elbow to hold your ear. contract your abdominal muscles and use your right elbow to get closer to the ground; pause briefly and return to the starting position.
15226.breathing: exhale when contracting and pressing down the abdominal muscles, and inhale when restoring.
15226.key_points: feel a sense of contraction and force in the right side of the abdomen when pressing down.
15226.mistakes:

solution: slow down the movement speed, and feel the strength of your abdominal muscles.
15226.notes:
inhale upward, twist, and lengthen the torso to one side.
tighten the abdominal muscles and keep your back straight throughout.

15232.name: Left-side Knee Raise And Abdominal Muscles Contract
15232.description: keep your weight on your right foot and put your right hand on your hip; put your left tiptoes on the ground, lift your left shoulder and stretch your left arm above your head, feeling the stretch in your left abdominal muscle. lift the left knee while pressing the left shoulder down and touching the left knee with the left elbow; then restore to the initial state after a pause.

15232.key_points: there is a sense of contraction and force in your left abdominal muscles.
15232.mistakes:

15232.notes: keep your weight on your right foot.

15238.description: kneel on the mat with knees hip-width apart and keep your knees below the hips. keep your hands shoulder-width apart, and put your hands on the mat. keep your spine natural, and stretch your head out. when exhaling, tighten your abdominal muscles and keep the body stable while stretching your right leg straight and back. when inhaling, bend your knees slowly to restore.

15250.name: Shoulder Bridge
15250.description: lie on your back with your legs naturally bent about 90 degrees, keep your legs hip-width apart, and relax your feet. place your hands naturally on both sides of your body with palms down, and keep your spine in a standard neutral position. when inhaling, keep your body stable, and when exhaling, contract the abdominal muscles, pull your navel toward the spine, tilt the pelvis backward and lift your pubis. continue to exhale, raise your spine from the tailbone section by section to roll off the mat until your knees and hips are raised in a straight line with the shoulders. inhale again, and keep your torso still. exhale, relax your chest and ribs, and turn the spine to the starting position, section by section.
15250.breathing:
when inhaling, keep your torso moving.
when exhaling, contract your abdominal muscles and move your spine section by section.
15250.key_points: step evenly and forcefully on the mat with both feet, and keep the body stable by tightening your hips and abdominal muscles when you lift your body.
15250.mistakes:
mistake: keep your knees spread out after you lift your body.
solution: keep your knees in the same direction as your tiptoes.

15298.name: Right Leg Reverse Lunge

15382.name: High Knee

15400.name: Svend Press
15400.description: stand shoulder-width apart, tighten your abdominal muscles, clamp the barbell piece in front of the chest with both hands, lift your chest and sink your shoulders. push both hands forward and hold them in the maximum position for 1 second, then restore to the starting position.
15400.breathing: inhale when restoring, and exhale when pushing.
15400.key_points:
keep your chest tight at all times. 
when pushing out, the chest has a strong sense of contraction and compression.
15400.mistakes:
mistake: use insufficient power to clamp the barbell piece.
solution: clamp the barbell piece in front of your chest firmly.
15400.notes:
keep your chest out and shoulders down to keep the shoulder blades stable.
tighten the abdominal muscles to keep your core stable.
keep your chest tense.

15406.name: Kneeling Push-ups
15406.description: cross your feet, kneel on the mat, keep your back straight, keep your body in a straight line from the side, and put your hands on both sides of the chest, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. bend your arms and bend down until your elbows are slightly above your torso, then stretch your arms and get up to restore.
15406.breathing: inhale when bending arms, and exhale when stretching arms.
15406.key_points: there is a feeling of soreness and swelling in the chest, the front of shoulders and the back of big arms.
15406.mistakes:
mistake: lock your elbow joint when stretching the arm, and collapse your waist or lift your hips during the training.
solution: keep the elbow joint straight, but do not lock it by overextension, keep your waist and back straight throughout the training, and keep your body in a straight line from the side.
15406.notes:
keep your fingertips forward.
draw your elbows in a bit, about 70 degrees with your torso.
keep your abdominal muscles tight, and do not collapse your waist.
when you push up, you should mainly contract and squeeze the chest.

15412.name: Standing Straight-arm Chest Press With Resistance Band
15412.description: open your arms horizontally, wrap the resistance band around your back, hook it on your thumbs, stand naturally on your feet, and keep your chest out and your abdominal muscles contracted. do a chest clenching movement with straight arms coming inward, stay for a while when your hands touch, and then restore. keep your shoulders and arms fixed throughout the whole process.
15412.breathing: inhale when restoring and exhale when your chest clenching.
15412.key_points: there is a clear sense of contraction and force in the chest.
15412.mistakes:
mistake: move your shoulder joint back and forth to borrow force
solution: keep your chest out, sink your shoulders, keep your shoulders away from the ears, and ensure that your shoulder joints are stable and still during the movement.

15413.name: Standing Straight-arm Chest Press With Resistance Band
15413.description: open your arms horizontally, wrap the resistance band around your back, hook it on your thumbs, stand naturally on your feet, and keep your chest out and your abdominal muscles contracted. do a chest clenching movement with straight arms coming inward, stay for a while when your hands touch, and then restore. keep your shoulders and arms fixed throughout the whole process.
15413.breathing: inhale when restoring and exhale when your chest clenching.
15413.key_points: there is a clear sense of contraction and force in the chest.
15413.mistakes:
mistake: move your shoulder joint back and forth to borrow force
solution: keep your chest out, sink your shoulders, keep your shoulders away from the ears, and ensure that your shoulder joints are stable and still during the movement.

15418.name: Small Dumbbell Floor Flies
15418.description: lie flat on your yoga mat, bend your knees, spread your legs shoulder-width apart, and keep your feet firmly planted on the ground. sink your shoulder blades so that your upper back is flat against the mat. hold the dumbbells with both hands opposite each other, place them right above your chest with your fists facing each other and keep your arms perpendicular to the ground. bend your elbows slightly, open your arms, lower the dumbbells to the ground, pause briefly and return to the starting position. control the movement speed when lowering the dumbbells, and do not touch the ground; do not collide the dumbbells when your arms fold.
15418.breathing: exhale when the arms are folded and inhale when they are lowered.
15418.key_points: when the force is launched, clamp the big arm inward, and there is a clear sense of contraction in the chest; at the highest point, there is a strong sense of compression in the chest. when launching the force, the front side of your shoulder assists the force with a slight sense of contraction. when descending to the lowest point, the chest feels slightly pulled.
15418.mistakes:
mistake: shrug your shoulders when powering up, and move your shoulders forward to borrow power
solution: sink your shoulders actively, contract your shoulder blades down and hold on all the time.
15418.notes: lower your big arms to the ground, and slightly bend your arms.

15424.name: Chest Fly
15424.description: raise your head, keep your chest out, and tighten your abdominal muscles. keep your palms forward and open your arms alternately at the same time.
15424.breathing: exhale with palms together, and inhale with chest expansion.
15424.key_points: feel the stretch in your chest
15424.mistakes:
mistake: move too fast or too rigid.
solution: relax your arms and open and close them in rhythm with your breath.
15424.notes:
keep your waist and abdominal muscles tight, and keep your body stable.
keep the palms of your hands forward.
breathe naturally and stretch your arms diagonally.

15430.name: Push-ups
15430.description: push up on the mat, keep your waist and back straight, keep your body in a straight line from the side, and hold the hands on both sides of the chest, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. bend your arms and bend down your body until your elbows are slightly higher than your torso, then stretch your arms to get up and restore.
15430.breathing: inhale when bending arms and exhale when extending arms.
15430.key_points: there is a feeling of soreness and swelling in the chest, the front shoulder and the back of the big arms.
15430.mistakes:
mistake: lock your elbow joint when stretching the arm, and collapse your waist or lift your hips during the training.
solution: keep your elbow joint straight, but do not lock it by overextension, keep your waist and back straight throughout the training, and keep your body in a straight line from the side.
15430.notes: keep your waist and back straight.

15436.name: Bent-over W-shape Stretch
15436.description: bend your knees and bend down, keep your body at an angle of 30° to 45° to the ground, bend your elbows, and clench your fists with thumbs outward. extend your arms to a w-shape with your body, relax your shoulders, clench your elbows, and feel the muscles of your mid-back and the middle of your back being squeezed. straighten your back, and keep your head in a straight line with your spine.
15436.breathing: exhale when stretching, and inhale when restoring.
15436.key_points: when the force is released, the middle back has a distinct squeezing sensation.
15436.mistakes:
mistake: did not take the shoulder as the axis when tightening the back backward, and spread out your elbows.
solution: keep the elbow clamped throughout the whole process.
mistake: bend and arch your back.
solution: tighten the core of the waist and abdominal muscles, and keep your back straight.
15436.notes:
clamp the elbows inward.
keep your chest out and clamp the shoulder blades.

15502.name: Bare-handed Cuban Press
15502.description: stand naturally, keep your chest out and stomach in, and place your fists in the front of your thighs. lift your arms until your big arms are parallel to the ground, keep your small arms at a 90-degree angle to your big arms and a 45-degree angle to the ground, with your fists down. using the upper arm as the axis, rotate the small arm upward until it is perpendicular to the ground. push up the arm with your fist forward and bring your arms closer to the middle. lower your big arm until it is parallel to the ground, and the small arm is at a 90-degree angle to the big arm. using the big arm as the axis, rotate the small arm downward to a 45-degree angle with the ground. lower your arms to the front of your thighs.
15502.breathing: exhale when you raise your arms and inhale when you lower your arms.
15502.key_points: there is a clear sense of contraction in the middle and back of the shoulder and in the area between the big arm and the back, but there is no sense of strong force.
15502.mistakes:
mistake: too fast.
solution: pause slightly after each stage of the action.
15502.notes:
lift the elbow and keep the big arm parallel to the ground.
do not shrug your shoulders.

15514.name: Dumbbell Curls
15514.description: stand naturally, keep your chest up and contract your abdominal muscles. clench your hips, keep your body stable, and keep your shoulders back and down, away from your ears. hold the dumbbells in both hands with the palms facing forward, and keep the big arms close to the body and fixed. with the front of the big arms forces, bend the arms and lift the dumbbells until they are close to the chest, pause briefly, and squeeze the arms. slowly unload the force and return to the starting position, and do not fully relax at the lowest point and do not fully straighten the arms. keep the arms fixed and close to the body during the movement.
15514.breathing: exhale when bending, and inhale when falling.
15514.key_points:
when bending, there is a clear sense of contraction on the front side of the big arm.
when falling to the lowest point, the whole arm feels tight.
15514.mistakes:
mistake: when bending, the body swings back and forth to borrow strength, resulting in poor training effect and discomfort in the waist.
solution: control the movement speed, maintain muscle control, do not swing the dumbbells, tighten your hips and abdomen, stabilize the body, and reduce the weight of the dumbbells if the weight is too heavy.
mistake: shrug your shoulders, and swing your body up and down
solution: always keep your chest up and your shoulders away from your ears as much as possible.
15514.notes:
keep your chest up and shoulders down, and keep your shoulder blades and shoulder joints stable and still.
keep your big arms close to your body and fixed.
tighten the abdomen and keep the core stable.
do not completely relax at the lowest point, and do not fully straighten your arms.

15521.description: keep your feet together, tighten your abdominal muscles, and sink your shoulders. hold the dumbbells in both hands on both sides of your body with your fists facing each other. the force is mainly generated by the elbow joint. bend one arm to lift the dumbbell until it is close to the chest while rotating the arm to bring the fist upward; pause for a moment. during the movement, keep your eyes on the front of the big arm on that side. slowly unload the force and return to the starting position, do not fully relax at the lowest point and do not fully straighten the arm; pause briefly to do the other side of the lift.
15521.breathing: exhale when bending, and inhale when falling.
15521.key_points:
when bending, there is a clear sense of contraction on the front side of the big arm.
when falling to the lowest point, the whole arm feels tight.
15521.mistakes:
mistake: when bending, the body swings back and forth to borrow strength, resulting in poor training effect and discomfort in the waist.
solution: reduce the weight of the dumbbells; or bend forward slightly.
15521.notes:
tighten the waist and abdominal muscles to keep the body stable.
keep your chest up and sink your shoulders.

15526.name: Right-side Kettlebell Bent-over Row
15526.description: support your left hand on your left knee, the left foot steps on the ground in a diagonal backward direction, and keep your back straight. lead your right shoulder forward, hold the dumbbell, and keep your arms perpendicular to the ground. use your back to force and pull your big arms backward and upward against the body until the elbows are slightly above the torso, and stop briefly at the highest point. unload the force slowly, restore to the starting position, and do not fully relax at the lowest point.
15526.breathing: inhale when lowering, and exhale when pulling up.
15526.key_points:
when pulling up, the back has a distinct sense of contraction, and at the highest point, there is a certain sense of squeezing.
when falling to the lowest point, the back feels slightly pulled.
15526.mistakes:
mistake: at the lowest point, the shoulder is not pulled forward, resulting in inadequate force on the back when pulling up.
solution: at the lowest point, lean your shoulder forward to open the scapula.

15538.name: Right-side Bent-over Tricep Extension With Resistance Band
15538.description: stand with your feet apart and step on the resistance band, bend your hips and stoop about 70°. hold the left arm on the knee to stabilize the body, and clamp the body with the right arm to pull the resistance band. make sure only the right small arm is in motion all over the body, and tense your arm for 1 second when it is straight.
15538.breathing: exhale when the arm is straightened and inhale when restored.
15538.key_points:
there is a distinct sense of contraction at the back of the upper arm when the force is applied.
keep the erector spine muscle and the back of the shoulder tight throughout.
15538.mistakes:
mistake: swing your body to borrow strength, bend, and stoop.
solution: tighten the waist and abdominal muscles throughout the process, straighten your back and slow down the movement.

15544.name: Bent-over Dumbbell Tricep Extension
15544.description: stand naturally, bend your knees slightly, try to bend over until your back is parallel to the ground, and tighten your waist and abdominal muscles. hold the dumbbells with both hands, and clamp the big arms against both sides of the body. straighten your arms, pause briefly and bend your elbows until your small arms are perpendicular to the ground.
15544.breathing: exhale when you straighten your arm and inhale when you bend your elbow and put down the dumbbell.
15544.key_points:
keep your lower back tense throughout the movement.
when you straighten your arm, you will feel a distinct contraction on the back of your big arm; you may feel a slight burning sensation after many times.
15544.mistakes:
mistake: arch your back, and swing your big arms up and down.
solution: reduce the bending range, keep the whole back straight; clamp your big arms simultaneously, keep them close to the sides of the body throughout.
15544.notes:
bend down, tighten your waist and abdominal muscles, and keep your back straight.
straighten your elbows and clamp the body with big arms.
bend your knees.

15550.name: Nod And Raise Head
15550.description: sit on the chair, put your hands on the thighs naturally, keep the waist and back straight, and keep your back close to the chair. put your hands behind the cervical spine to ensure the neck is fixed throughout the movement. when nodding your head, keep your lower jaw close to your neck, and when raising your head, raise your lower jaw upward.
15550.key_points:
when nodding your head, the muscles at the back of the neck feel slightly pulled.
when raising your head, the front muscles of the neck feel slightly pulled.
after the movement, there is a sense of stretching in the neck.
15550.mistakes:
mistake: your neck swings back and forth, following your head nodding and raising.
solution: hold the back side of the cervical spine with your hand and slowly complete the movement while keeping the cervical spine still.
15550.notes:
keep your neck fixed throughout the whole movement.
keep your head down and chin close to the neck.

15556.key_points: there is a sense of stretching on the front side of the neck.
15556.mistakes:

solution: turn your head slower and feel the stretch on the front side of your neck.

15562.name: Shrug And Sink The Shoulders
15562.description: stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, keep your chest up, stomach in, and shoulders down, and put your arms naturally on both sides of the body. raise your shoulder blades to the maximum extent, with a slight pause; then sink your shoulder blades to the maximum extent, with a slight pause; repeat the process in turn.
15562.breathing: shrug your shoulders and breathe in; sink your shoulders and breathe out.
15562.key_points:
when lifting up, you can't see your neck.
when sinking, you should feel the neck slender.
15562.mistakes:
mistake: too fast
solution: pause slightly after each stage of the action.
15562.notes: keep your shoulders down to the lowest point.

15568.name: Four-way Nod Head
15568.description: sit on the chair, put your hands naturally on your thighs, and keep your waist straight and your back close to the chair. rotate your head forward, backward, leftward, and rightward in a particular order.

solution: slow down the action, and feel the muscle's strength and contraction.

15574.name: Lying Alternate Upper-half Leg Raise
15574.description: keep your waist close to the ground, lift your hips off the ground, and there is a sense of tightness in the lower abdomen. put your hands on both sides of the hips, hook up your toes, and lift your legs when they drop to about 45°, and there should be no tension in your waist. keep the knee joints of both legs fixed, and there should be no kicking action.
15574.key_points: keep your whole abdominal muscle tight throughout, and the longer the action lasts, the stronger the burning sensation of the abdominal muscles.
15574.mistakes:
mistake: the waist can not be on the ground.
solution: do not drop your legs too low.
15574.notes:
keep your waist close to the ground.
keep your abdominal muscles tight.

15580.name: Half Roll Back
15580.description: sit on the yoga mat, keep your legs slightly bent and hip-width apart, and keep your back straight. when inhaling, extend your head and spine towards the ceiling. when exhaling, roll your tailbone toward the pubis, tighten the pelvic floor muscles, tilt the pelvis backward, and slowly flex the spine backward. make your spine form a "c" with a sense of extension. inhale and return to the starting position.
15580.breathing:
inhale through the nose.
exhale through the mouth.
15580.key_points: tighten your pelvic floor muscles and abdominal muscles.
15580.mistakes:
mistake: your waist bulges back excessively.
solution: lean back your pelvis slightly and drive your spine as a whole to extend backward.
15580.notes:
exhale, roll the tailbone toward the pubis, tilt the pelvis backward and tighten the abdominal muscles.
keep your spine extended.

15586.name: Kneeling Right-side Torso Twist
15586.description: lie prone on a yoga mat with your knees on the ground and slightly apart; put your left hand on the ground and bend your right elbow to hold your ear. contract your abdominal muscles and use your right elbow to get closer to the ground; pause briefly and return to the starting position.
15586.breathing: exhale when contracting and pressing down the abdominal muscles, and inhale when restoring.
15586.key_points: feel a sense of contraction and force in the right side of the abdomen when pressing down.
15586.mistakes:
mistake: too fast.
solution: slow down the movement speed, and feel the strength of your abdominal muscles.
15586.notes:
inhale upward, twist, and lengthen the torso to one side.
tighten the abdominal muscles and keep your back straight throughout.

15592.name: Left-side Knee Raise And Abdominal Muscles Contract
15592.description: keep your weight on your right foot and put your right hand on your hip; put your left tiptoes on the ground, lift your left shoulder and stretch your left arm above your head, feeling the stretch in your left abdominal muscle. lift the left knee while pressing the left shoulder down and touching the left knee with the left elbow; then restore to the initial state after a pause.
15592.breathing: exhale when pressing down, and inhale when stretching.
15592.key_points: there is a sense of contraction and force in your left abdominal muscles.
15592.mistakes:
mistake: collide your elbows and knees in front of your body.
solution: lift your knee from the side and bend the body sideways instead of forward.
15592.notes: keep your weight on your right foot.

15610.name: Shoulder Bridge
15610.description: lie on your back with your legs naturally bent about 90 degrees, keep your legs hip-width apart, and relax your feet. place your hands naturally on both sides of your body with palms down, and keep your spine in a standard neutral position. when inhaling, keep your body stable, and when exhaling, contract the abdominal muscles, pull your navel toward the spine, tilt the pelvis backward and lift your pubis. continue to exhale, raise your spine from the tailbone section by section to roll off the mat until your knees and hips are raised in a straight line with the shoulders. inhale again, and keep your torso still. exhale, relax your chest and ribs, and turn the spine to the starting position, section by section.
15610.breathing:
when inhaling, keep your torso moving.
when exhaling, contract your abdominal muscles and move your spine section by section.
15610.key_points: step evenly and forcefully on the mat with both feet, and keep the body stable by tightening your hips and abdominal muscles when you lift your body.
15610.mistakes:
mistake: keep your knees spread out after you lift your body.
solution: keep your knees in the same direction as your tiptoes.
mistake: use your neck to support after the body lift.
solution: use your upper back to support, and do not press your neck.
mistake: lift your hips too high, and turn out your ribs.
solution: tighten your abdominal muscles, retract your ribs, and keep your knees, hips, and shoulders in a straight line.
15610.notes:
use your upper back to support.
tighten your abdominal muscles.
clamp your hips.

15646.name: Sit-ups
15646.description: lie on the mat, put your arms straight on either side of your head, put your feet together, open your legs, and use your abdominal muscles to get up. keep your head, shoulders, upper back, and lower back off the ground in turn, and touch your feet with your hands. make sure your lower back, upper back, shoulder, and head touch the ground in turn when lowering. control your speed throughout the action, with the frequency of about once every 2 seconds.

mistake: your waist is off the ground when you get up, causing pain.
solution: always relax your waist and stick it to the mat.
15646.notes:
lift your head, shoulders, upper back, and lower back off the ground in turn.

15658.name: Right Leg Reverse Lunge
15658.description: keep your chest up and your abdominal muscles tight, and look ahead with both hands on your hips. step back with your right leg, squat down so that the knee joint and ankle joint are in the same vertical line, and keep the load evenly distributed on both legs; sink your hip, bend the knees and squat down until your right leg knee joint is close to the ground, and then return.
15658.breathing: inhale when pressing down, and exhale when restoring.
15658.key_points: there is tension in your quadriceps femoris muscles.
15658.mistakes:
mistake: the body leans backward or forward, and your knees exceed the toes when squatting.
solution: always keep your upper body straight, squat with your front leg perpendicular to the ground, and your knees should not exceed your toes.

15688.name: Sumo Squat
15688.description: stand about twice shoulder-width apart, with your toes facing diagonally forward. when squatting to the thighs parallel to the ground, keep your knees in the same direction as your toes. keep your upper body as straight as possible, and sit back slightly when squatting. cross your arms over your chest.

15760.name: Svend Press
15760.description: stand shoulder-width apart, tighten your abdominal muscles, clamp the barbell piece in front of the chest with both hands, lift your chest and sink your shoulders. push both hands forward and hold them in the maximum position for 1 second, then restore to the starting position.
15760.breathing: inhale when restoring, and exhale when pushing.
15760.key_points:
keep your chest tight at all times. 
when pushing out, the chest has a strong sense of contraction and compression.
15760.mistakes:
mistake: use insufficient power to clamp the barbell piece.
solution: clamp the barbell piece in front of your chest firmly.
15760.notes:
keep your chest out and shoulders down to keep the shoulder blades stable.
tighten the abdominal muscles to keep your core stable.
keep your chest tense.

15766.name: Kneeling Push-ups
15766.description: cross your feet, kneel on the mat, keep your back straight, keep your body in a straight line from the side, and put your hands on both sides of the chest, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. bend your arms and bend down until your elbows are slightly above your torso, then stretch your arms and get up to restore.
15766.breathing: inhale when bending arms, and exhale when stretching arms.
15766.key_points: there is a feeling of soreness and swelling in the chest, the front of shoulders and the back of big arms.
15766.mistakes:
mistake: lock your elbow joint when stretching the arm, and collapse your waist or lift your hips during the training.
solution: keep the elbow joint straight, but do not lock it by overextension, keep your waist and back straight throughout the training, and keep your body in a straight line from the side.
15766.notes:
keep your fingertips forward.
draw your elbows in a bit, about 70 degrees with your torso.
keep your abdominal muscles tight, and do not collapse your waist.
when you push up, you should mainly contract and squeeze the chest.

15772.name: Standing Straight-arm Chest Press With Resistance Band
15772.description: open your arms horizontally, wrap the resistance band around your back, hook it on your thumbs, stand naturally on your feet, and keep your chest out and your abdominal muscles contracted. do a chest clenching movement with straight arms coming inward, stay for a while when your hands touch, and then restore. keep your shoulders and arms fixed throughout the whole process.
15772.breathing: inhale when restoring and exhale when your chest clenching.
15772.key_points: there is a clear sense of contraction and force in the chest.
15772.mistakes:
mistake: move your shoulder joint back and forth to borrow force
solution: keep your chest out, sink your shoulders, keep your shoulders away from the ears, and ensure that your shoulder joints are stable and still during the movement.

15778.name: Small Dumbbell Floor Flies
15778.description: lie flat on your yoga mat, bend your knees, spread your legs shoulder-width apart, and keep your feet firmly planted on the ground. sink your shoulder blades so that your upper back is flat against the mat. hold the dumbbells with both hands opposite each other, place them right above your chest with your fists facing each other and keep your arms perpendicular to the ground. bend your elbows slightly, open your arms, lower the dumbbells to the ground, pause briefly and return to the starting position. control the movement speed when lowering the dumbbells, and do not touch the ground; do not collide the dumbbells when your arms fold.
15778.breathing: exhale when the arms are folded and inhale when they are lowered.
15778.key_points: when the force is launched, clamp the big arm inward, and there is a clear sense of contraction in the chest; at the highest point, there is a strong sense of compression in the chest. when launching the force, the front side of your shoulder assists the force with a slight sense of contraction. when descending to the lowest point, the chest feels slightly pulled.
15778.mistakes:
mistake: shrug your shoulders when powering up, and move your shoulders forward to borrow power
solution: sink your shoulders actively, contract your shoulder blades down and hold on all the time.
15778.notes: lower your big arms to the ground, and slightly bend your arms.

15784.name: Chest Fly
15784.description: raise your head, keep your chest out, and tighten your abdominal muscles. keep your palms forward and open your arms alternately at the same time.
15784.breathing: exhale with palms together, and inhale with chest expansion.
15784.key_points: feel the stretch in your chest
15784.mistakes:
mistake: move too fast or too rigid.
solution: relax your arms and open and close them in rhythm with your breath.
15784.notes:
keep your waist and abdominal muscles tight, and keep your body stable.
keep the palms of your hands forward.
breathe naturally and stretch your arms diagonally.

15794.key_points: there is a feeling of soreness and swelling in the chest, the front shoulder and the back of the big arms.
15794.mistakes:
mistake: lock your elbow joint when stretching the arm, and collapse your waist or lift your hips during the training.
solution: keep your elbow joint straight, but do not lock it by overextension, keep your waist and back straight throughout the training, and keep your body in a straight line from the side.
15794.notes: keep your waist and back straight.

15796.name: Bent-over W-shape Stretch
15796.description: bend your knees and bend down, keep your body at an angle of 30° to 45° to the ground, bend your elbows, and clench your fists with thumbs outward. extend your arms to a w-shape with your body, relax your shoulders, clench your elbows, and feel the muscles of your mid-back and the middle of your back being squeezed. straighten your back, and keep your head in a straight line with your spine.
15796.breathing: exhale when stretching, and inhale when restoring.
15796.key_points: when the force is released, the middle back has a distinct squeezing sensation.
15796.mistakes:
mistake: did not take the shoulder as the axis when tightening the back backward, and spread out your elbows.
solution: keep the elbow clamped throughout the whole process.
mistake: bend and arch your back.
solution: tighten the core of the waist and abdominal muscles, and keep your back straight.
15796.notes:
clamp the elbows inward.
keep your chest out and clamp the shoulder blades.

15862.name: Bare-handed Cuban Press
15862.description: stand naturally, keep your chest out and stomach in, and place your fists in the front of your thighs. lift your arms until your big arms are parallel to the ground, keep your small arms at a 90-degree angle to your big arms and a 45-degree angle to the ground, with your fists down. using the upper arm as the axis, rotate the small arm upward until it is perpendicular to the ground. push up the arm with your fist forward and bring your arms closer to the middle. lower your big arm until it is parallel to the ground, and the small arm is at a 90-degree angle to the big arm. using the big arm as the axis, rotate the small arm downward to a 45-degree angle with the ground. lower your arms to the front of your thighs.
15862.breathing: exhale when you raise your arms and inhale when you lower your arms.
15862.key_points: there is a clear sense of contraction in the middle and back of the shoulder and in the area between the big arm and the back, but there is no sense of strong force.
15862.mistakes:
mistake: too fast.
solution: pause slightly after each stage of the action.
15862.notes:
lift the elbow and keep the big arm parallel to the ground.
do not shrug your shoulders.

15873.name: Fortune Cat
15873.description: stand naturally, keep your chest out, contract your abdominal muscles, and raise your big arm until it is parallel to the ground, the small arm at an angle of 90 degrees to the big arm and 45 degrees to the ground, with your palms down. using the big arm as the axis, rotate the small arm upward until it is perpendicular to the ground, and pause slightly. return to the starting position.

15874.name: Dumbbell Curls
15874.description: stand naturally, keep your chest up and contract your abdominal muscles. clench your hips, keep your body stable, and keep your shoulders back and down, away from your ears. hold the dumbbells in both hands with the palms facing forward, and keep the big arms close to the body and fixed. with the front of the big arms forces, bend the arms and lift the dumbbells until they are close to the chest, pause briefly, and squeeze the arms. slowly unload the force and return to the starting position, and do not fully relax at the lowest point and do not fully straighten the arms. keep the arms fixed and close to the body during the movement.
15874.breathing: exhale when bending, and inhale when falling.

solution: always keep your chest up and your shoulders away from your ears as much as possible.

15880.name: Alternate Dumbbell Curls
15880.description: keep your feet together, tighten your abdominal muscles, and sink your shoulders. hold the dumbbells in both hands on both sides of your body with your fists facing each other. the force is mainly generated by the elbow joint. bend one arm to lift the dumbbell until it is close to the chest while rotating the arm to bring the fist upward; pause for a moment. during the movement, keep your eyes on the front of the big arm on that side. slowly unload the force and return to the starting position, do not fully relax at the lowest point and do not fully straighten the arm; pause briefly to do the other side of the lift.

15880.notes:
tighten the waist and abdominal muscles to keep the body stable.
keep your chest up and sink your shoulders.

15886.name: Right-side Kettlebell Bent-over Row
15886.description: support your left hand on your left knee, the left foot steps on the ground in a diagonal backward direction, and keep your back straight. lead your right shoulder forward, hold the dumbbell, and keep your arms perpendicular to the ground. use your back to force and pull your big arms backward and upward against the body until the elbows are slightly above the torso, and stop briefly at the highest point. unload the force slowly, restore to the starting position, and do not fully relax at the lowest point.
15886.breathing: inhale when lowering, and exhale when pulling up.
15886.key_points:
when pulling up, the back has a distinct sense of contraction, and at the highest point, there is a certain sense of squeezing.
when falling to the lowest point, the back feels slightly pulled.
15886.mistakes:
mistake: at the lowest point, the shoulder is not pulled forward, resulting in inadequate force on the back when pulling up.
solution: at the lowest point, lean your shoulder forward to open the scapula.

15898.name: Right-side Bent-over Tricep Extension With Resistance Band
15898.description: stand with your feet apart and step on the resistance band, bend your hips and stoop about 70°. hold the left arm on the knee to stabilize the body, and clamp the body with the right arm to pull the resistance band. make sure only the right small arm is in motion all over the body, and tense your arm for 1 second when it is straight.
15898.breathing: exhale when the arm is straightened and inhale when restored.
15898.key_points:
there is a distinct sense of contraction at the back of the upper arm when the force is applied.
keep the erector spine muscle and the back of the shoulder tight throughout.
15898.mistakes:
mistake: swing your body to borrow strength, bend, and stoop.
solution: tighten the waist and abdominal muscles throughout the process, straighten your back and slow down the movement.

15910.name: Nod And Raise Head
15910.description: sit on the chair, put your hands on the thighs naturally, keep the waist and back straight, and keep your back close to the chair. put your hands behind the cervical spine to ensure the neck is fixed throughout the movement. when nodding your head, keep your lower jaw close to your neck, and when raising your head, raise your lower jaw upward.
15910.key_points:
when nodding your head, the muscles at the back of the neck feel slightly pulled.
when raising your head, the front muscles of the neck feel slightly pulled.
after the movement, there is a sense of stretching in the neck.
15910.mistakes:
mistake: your neck swings back and forth, following your head nodding and raising.
solution: hold the back side of the cervical spine with your hand and slowly complete the movement while keeping the cervical spine still.
15910.notes:
keep your neck fixed throughout the whole movement.
keep your head down and chin close to the neck.

15916.name: Two-way Head Turn
15916.description: sit in a chair, put your hands naturally on your thighs, and keep your waist straight and your back close to the chair. turn your head to one side, stay for a while, then turn back, and then turn to the other side. try your best to look behind when you turn your head, which will increase the pulling sensation of the neck.
15916.key_points: there is a sense of stretching on the front side of the neck.
15916.mistakes:

solution: turn your head slower and feel the stretch on the front side of your neck.
15916.notes: turn your head to one side and try to look behind your body.

15922.name: Shrug And Sink The Shoulders
15922.description: stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, keep your chest up, stomach in, and shoulders down, and put your arms naturally on both sides of the body. raise your shoulder blades to the maximum extent, with a slight pause; then sink your shoulder blades to the maximum extent, with a slight pause; repeat the process in turn.
15922.breathing: shrug your shoulders and breathe in; sink your shoulders and breathe out.
15922.key_points:
when lifting up, you can't see your neck.
when sinking, you should feel the neck slender.
15922.mistakes:
mistake: too fast
solution: pause slightly after each stage of the action.
15922.notes: keep your shoulders down to the lowest point.

15928.name: Four-way Nod Head

15934.name: Lying Alternate Upper-half Leg Raise
15934.description: keep your waist close to the ground, lift your hips off the ground, and there is a sense of tightness in the lower abdomen. put your hands on both sides of the hips, hook up your toes, and lift your legs when they drop to about 45°, and there should be no tension in your waist. keep the knee joints of both legs fixed, and there should be no kicking action.
15934.key_points: keep your whole abdominal muscle tight throughout, and the longer the action lasts, the stronger the burning sensation of the abdominal muscles.
15934.mistakes:
mistake: the waist can not be on the ground.
solution: do not drop your legs too low.
15934.notes:
keep your waist close to the ground.
keep your abdominal muscles tight.

15940.name: Half Roll Back
15940.description: sit on the yoga mat, keep your legs slightly bent and hip-width apart, and keep your back straight. when inhaling, extend your head and spine towards the ceiling. when exhaling, roll your tailbone toward the pubis, tighten the pelvic floor muscles, tilt the pelvis backward, and slowly flex the spine backward. make your spine form a "c" with a sense of extension. inhale and return to the starting position.
15940.breathing:
inhale through the nose.
exhale through the mouth.
15940.key_points: tighten your pelvic floor muscles and abdominal muscles.
15940.mistakes:
mistake: your waist bulges back excessively.
solution: lean back your pelvis slightly and drive your spine as a whole to extend backward.
15940.notes:
exhale, roll the tailbone toward the pubis, tilt the pelvis backward and tighten the abdominal muscles.
keep your spine extended.

15970.name: Shoulder Bridge
15970.description: lie on your back with your legs naturally bent about 90 degrees, keep your legs hip-width apart, and relax your feet. place your hands naturally on both sides of your body with palms down, and keep your spine in a standard neutral position. when inhaling, keep your body stable, and when exhaling, contract the abdominal muscles, pull your navel toward the spine, tilt the pelvis backward and lift your pubis. continue to exhale, raise your spine from the tailbone section by section to roll off the mat until your knees and hips are raised in a straight line with the shoulders. inhale again, and keep your torso still. exhale, relax your chest and ribs, and turn the spine to the starting position, section by section.
15970.breathing:
when inhaling, keep your torso moving.
when exhaling, contract your abdominal muscles and move your spine section by section.
15970.key_points: step evenly and forcefully on the mat with both feet, and keep the body stable by tightening your hips and abdominal muscles when you lift your body.
15970.mistakes:
mistake: keep your knees spread out after you lift your body.
solution: keep your knees in the same direction as your tiptoes.
mistake: use your neck to support after the body lift.
solution: use your upper back to support, and do not press your neck.
mistake: lift your hips too high, and turn out your ribs.
solution: tighten your abdominal muscles, retract your ribs, and keep your knees, hips, and shoulders in a straight line.
15970.notes:
use your upper back to support.
tighten your abdominal muscles.
clamp your hips.

16006.name: Sit-ups
16006.description: lie on the mat, put your arms straight on either side of your head, put your feet together, open your legs, and use your abdominal muscles to get up. keep your head, shoulders, upper back, and lower back off the ground in turn, and touch your feet with your hands. make sure your lower back, upper back, shoulder, and head touch the ground in turn when lowering. control your speed throughout the action, with the frequency of about once every 2 seconds.
16006.breathing: inhale when lowering, and exhale when rising.
16006.key_points:
there is a sudden sense of contraction and tightness in your abdomen when rising, and there is a squeezing sensation in your abdomen in the second half of your rise.
relax your waist all the time, and there should be no tightness.
16006.mistakes:
mistake: your waist is off the ground when you get up, causing pain.
solution: always relax your waist and stick it to the mat.
16006.notes:
lift your head, shoulders, upper back, and lower back off the ground in turn.
use your abdominal muscles.

16101.breathing: inhale when lifting arms and exhale when lowering.
16101.key_points:
relax your ankles and knees, and always keep your abdomen tight.
maintain some overall elasticity.
16101.mistakes:
mistake: the movement is too slow, causing your waist and abdomen to become loose.
solution: speed up the movement.
16101.notes: swing your arms quickly to drive the body to jump.

16102.name: High Knee
16102.description: straighten your back, look ahead, and lift your legs alternately and quickly with your front feet on the ground. keep your body stable and swing your arms with the rhythm of the leg lifts. maintain the fastest speed.
16102.key_points: the faster the speed, the faster the heartbeat, and the faster the breathing.
16102.mistakes:
mistake: shift your weight backward.
solution: reduce the range of the leg lift, and keep the body stable.
16102.notes:
lean your upper body slightly forward.
retract your abdominal muscles.
lift your legs as fast as you can.

16108.name: Clap Jacks
16108.description: lift your head and chest, and tense your abdomen. tense the arms, and use the strength of your pectoral muscles to clap your hands while jumping back and forth with alternating feet.
16108.breathing: exhale when you clap your hands, and inhale when you expand your chest.
16108.key_points: keep your movement light and your body flexible and not stiff.
16108.mistakes:
mistake: the movement is too slow, causing your waist and abdomen to become loose.
solution: speed up the movement.
16108.notes:
open your arms horizontally.
do not relax your shoulders.

16114.name: Run In Place With Arm Swing
16114.description: lean your upper body forward slightly. clench your fists, swing your arms as fast as possible, and lift your legs alternately and quickly while swinging your arms, like a sprint run. keep your torso as stable as possible.
16114.key_points: there is a sense of stretching in your shoulders, chest, and back. the heartbeat is very fast, and the breathing is tight.
16114.mistakes:
mistake: the foot landing sounds too loud, and the foot landing is not controlled.
solution: the landing sound should be lighter to reduce the impact on your lower limb joints.

16120.name: Svend Press
16120.description: stand shoulder-width apart, tighten your abdominal muscles, clamp the barbell piece in front of the chest with both hands, lift your chest and sink your shoulders. push both hands forward and hold them in the maximum position for 1 second, then restore to the starting position.
16120.breathing: inhale when restoring, and exhale when pushing.
16120.key_points:
keep your chest tight at all times. 
when pushing out, the chest has a strong sense of contraction and compression.
16120.mistakes:
mistake: use insufficient power to clamp the barbell piece.
solution: clamp the barbell piece in front of your chest firmly.
16120.notes:
keep your chest out and shoulders down to keep the shoulder blades stable.
tighten the abdominal muscles to keep your core stable.
keep your chest tense.

16126.name: Kneeling Push-ups
16126.description: cross your feet, kneel on the mat, keep your back straight, keep your body in a straight line from the side, and put your hands on both sides of the chest, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. bend your arms and bend down until your elbows are slightly above your torso, then stretch your arms and get up to restore.
16126.breathing: inhale when bending arms, and exhale when stretching arms.
16126.key_points: there is a feeling of soreness and swelling in the chest, the front of shoulders and the back of big arms.
16126.mistakes:
mistake: lock your elbow joint when stretching the arm, and collapse your waist or lift your hips during the training.
solution: keep the elbow joint straight, but do not lock it by overextension, keep your waist and back straight throughout the training, and keep your body in a straight line from the side.
16126.notes:
keep your fingertips forward.
draw your elbows in a bit, about 70 degrees with your torso.
keep your abdominal muscles tight, and do not collapse your waist.
when you push up, you should mainly contract and squeeze the chest.

16132.name: Standing Straight-arm Chest Press With Resistance Band
16132.description: open your arms horizontally, wrap the resistance band around your back, hook it on your thumbs, stand naturally on your feet, and keep your chest out and your abdominal muscles contracted. do a chest clenching movement with straight arms coming inward, stay for a while when your hands touch, and then restore. keep your shoulders and arms fixed throughout the whole process.
16132.breathing: inhale when restoring and exhale when your chest clenching.
16132.key_points: there is a clear sense of contraction and force in the chest.
16132.mistakes:
mistake: move your shoulder joint back and forth to borrow force
solution: keep your chest out, sink your shoulders, keep your shoulders away from the ears, and ensure that your shoulder joints are stable and still during the movement.

16138.name: Small Dumbbell Floor Flies
16138.description: lie flat on your yoga mat, bend your knees, spread your legs shoulder-width apart, and keep your feet firmly planted on the ground. sink your shoulder blades so that your upper back is flat against the mat. hold the dumbbells with both hands opposite each other, place them right above your chest with your fists facing each other and keep your arms perpendicular to the ground. bend your elbows slightly, open your arms, lower the dumbbells to the ground, pause briefly and return to the starting position. control the movement speed when lowering the dumbbells, and do not touch the ground; do not collide the dumbbells when your arms fold.
16138.breathing: exhale when the arms are folded and inhale when they are lowered.
16138.key_points: when the force is launched, clamp the big arm inward, and there is a clear sense of contraction in the chest; at the highest point, there is a strong sense of compression in the chest. when launching the force, the front side of your shoulder assists the force with a slight sense of contraction. when descending to the lowest point, the chest feels slightly pulled.
16138.mistakes:
mistake: shrug your shoulders when powering up, and move your shoulders forward to borrow power
solution: sink your shoulders actively, contract your shoulder blades down and hold on all the time.
16138.notes: lower your big arms to the ground, and slightly bend your arms.

16141.description: lie flat on your yoga mat, bend your knees, spread your legs shoulder-width apart, and keep your feet firmly planted on the ground. sink your shoulder blades so that your upper back is flat against the mat. hold the dumbbells with both hands opposite each other, place them right above your chest with your fists facing each other and keep your arms perpendicular to the ground. bend your elbows slightly, open your arms, lower the dumbbells to the ground, pause briefly and return to the starting position. control the movement speed when lowering the dumbbells, and do not touch the ground; do not collide the dumbbells when your arms fold.
16141.breathing: exhale when the arms are folded and inhale when they are lowered.

16150.name: Push-ups
16150.description: push up on the mat, keep your waist and back straight, keep your body in a straight line from the side, and hold the hands on both sides of the chest, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. bend your arms and bend down your body until your elbows are slightly higher than your torso, then stretch your arms to get up and restore.
16150.breathing: inhale when bending arms and exhale when extending arms.

16150.mistakes:
mistake: lock your elbow joint when stretching the arm, and collapse your waist or lift your hips during the training.
solution: keep your elbow joint straight, but do not lock it by overextension, keep your waist and back straight throughout the training, and keep your body in a straight line from the side.
16150.notes: keep your waist and back straight.

16156.name: Bent-over W-shape Stretch
16156.description: bend your knees and bend down, keep your body at an angle of 30° to 45° to the ground, bend your elbows, and clench your fists with thumbs outward. extend your arms to a w-shape with your body, relax your shoulders, clench your elbows, and feel the muscles of your mid-back and the middle of your back being squeezed. straighten your back, and keep your head in a straight line with your spine.
16156.breathing: exhale when stretching, and inhale when restoring.
16156.key_points: when the force is released, the middle back has a distinct squeezing sensation.
16156.mistakes:
mistake: did not take the shoulder as the axis when tightening the back backward, and spread out your elbows.
solution: keep the elbow clamped throughout the whole process.
mistake: bend and arch your back.
solution: tighten the core of the waist and abdominal muscles, and keep your back straight.
16156.notes:
clamp the elbows inward.
keep your chest out and clamp the shoulder blades.

16176.breathing: inhale when lifting the arm, and exhale when restoring.
16176.key_points: the thoracic spine twists to a certain extent, and the chest on the hand-raising side feels slightly pulled.
16176.mistakes:
mistake: lower limbs follow upper limbs to turn.
solution: keep the other arm against the inside of the knee to prevent the lower limb from following the upper body rotation.
16176.notes:
squat entirely and relax your legs.
keep your waist and back straight.
keep your arms in front of your knees.

16180.name: Breaststroke Arm Pull
16180.description: lie prone on the mat with your abdomen and hips on the mat, lift your chest and legs, and stretch your arms forward. straighten your waist and back, clamp your shoulders, and move your arms backward to the sides of your thighs for a while. open your shoulders and move your arms forward to the initial position.
16180.breathing: inhale when rowing backward and exhale when rowing forward.
16180.key_points: there is a feeling of soreness and swelling in the back and the shoulders.
16180.mistakes:
mistake: put your chest and legs on the ground, but not clamp your shoulders when rowing backward.
solution: lift your chest and legs, and clamp the shoulders when the arms row backward.

16186.name: Prone Y-shape Stretch
16186.description: lie prone on the yoga mat with your arms in a y-shape with your body, clench your hands in fists and keep your thumbs up. do not leave your ribs off the ground, lift your thumbs and feel the strength of your mid-back muscles.
16186.breathing: exhale when forcing, and inhale when restoring.
16186.key_points: when lifting, the lower back is tight and contracted, and the middle back feels squeezing towards the center.
16186.mistakes:
mistake: the waist feels more intense
solution: keep your abdominal muscles contracted, keep your abdomen slightly off the ground, and adjust the upper body's weight to the lower edge of your ribs.

16192.name: Lateral Raise Forward Circles
16192.description: stand on your feet naturally, and keep your chest out, stomach in, and shoulders down. Raise your arms horizontally with your palm upward, stretch your fingers as far as possible, and always keep this outward feeling. with the shoulder joint as the axis, the upper arm rotates forward slightly around the shoulder joint.
16192.key_points: there is a sense of soreness and swelling in the shoulders.
16192.mistakes:
mistake: cannot keep arms parallel to the ground all the time.
solution: keep your chest out and stomach in, and keep the fingers outward all the time
16192.notes:
relax your shoulders and do not shrug your shoulders.
straighten your arms naturally.

16222.name: Bare-handed Cuban Press
16222.description: stand naturally, keep your chest out and stomach in, and place your fists in the front of your thighs. lift your arms until your big arms are parallel to the ground, keep your small arms at a 90-degree angle to your big arms and a 45-degree angle to the ground, with your fists down. using the upper arm as the axis, rotate the small arm upward until it is perpendicular to the ground. push up the arm with your fist forward and bring your arms closer to the middle. lower your big arm until it is parallel to the ground, and the small arm is at a 90-degree angle to the big arm. using the big arm as the axis, rotate the small arm downward to a 45-degree angle with the ground. lower your arms to the front of your thighs.

solution: pause slightly after each stage of the action.

lift the elbow and keep the big arm parallel to the ground.
do not shrug your shoulders.

16234.name: Dumbbell Curls
16234.description: stand naturally, keep your chest up and contract your abdominal muscles. clench your hips, keep your body stable, and keep your shoulders back and down, away from your ears. hold the dumbbells in both hands with the palms facing forward, and keep the big arms close to the body and fixed. with the front of the big arms forces, bend the arms and lift the dumbbells until they are close to the chest, pause briefly, and squeeze the arms. slowly unload the force and return to the starting position, and do not fully relax at the lowest point and do not fully straighten the arms. keep the arms fixed and close to the body during the movement.
16234.breathing: exhale when bending, and inhale when falling.
16234.key_points:
when bending, there is a clear sense of contraction on the front side of the big arm.
when falling to the lowest point, the whole arm feels tight.
16234.mistakes:
mistake: when bending, the body swings back and forth to borrow strength, resulting in poor training effect and discomfort in the waist.
solution: control the movement speed, maintain muscle control, do not swing the dumbbells, tighten your hips and abdomen, stabilize the body, and reduce the weight of the dumbbells if the weight is too heavy.
mistake: shrug your shoulders, and swing your body up and down
solution: always keep your chest up and your shoulders away from your ears as much as possible.
16234.notes:
keep your chest up and shoulders down, and keep your shoulder blades and shoulder joints stable and still.
keep your big arms close to your body and fixed.
tighten the abdomen and keep the core stable.
do not completely relax at the lowest point, and do not fully straighten your arms.

16246.name: Right-side Kettlebell Bent-over Row
16246.description: support your left hand on your left knee, the left foot steps on the ground in a diagonal backward direction, and keep your back straight. lead your right shoulder forward, hold the dumbbell, and keep your arms perpendicular to the ground. use your back to force and pull your big arms backward and upward against the body until the elbows are slightly above the torso, and stop briefly at the highest point. unload the force slowly, restore to the starting position, and do not fully relax at the lowest point.
16246.breathing: inhale when lowering, and exhale when pulling up.
16246.key_points:
when pulling up, the back has a distinct sense of contraction, and at the highest point, there is a certain sense of squeezing.
when falling to the lowest point, the back feels slightly pulled.
16246.mistakes:
mistake: at the lowest point, the shoulder is not pulled forward, resulting in inadequate force on the back when pulling up.
solution: at the lowest point, lean your shoulder forward to open the scapula.

16247.breathing: inhale when lowering, and exhale when pulling up.
16247.key_points:
when pulling up, the back has a distinct sense of contraction, and at the highest point, there is a certain sense of squeezing.
when falling to the lowest point, the back feels slightly pulled.
16247.mistakes:
mistake: at the lowest point, the shoulder is not pulled forward, resulting in inadequate force on the back when pulling up.

16258.name: Right-side Bent-over Tricep Extension With Resistance Band
16258.description: stand with your feet apart and step on the resistance band, bend your hips and stoop about 70°. hold the left arm on the knee to stabilize the body, and clamp the body with the right arm to pull the resistance band. make sure only the right small arm is in motion all over the body, and tense your arm for 1 second when it is straight.
16258.breathing: exhale when the arm is straightened and inhale when restored.
16258.key_points:
there is a distinct sense of contraction at the back of the upper arm when the force is applied.
keep the erector spine muscle and the back of the shoulder tight throughout.
16258.mistakes:
mistake: swing your body to borrow strength, bend, and stoop.
solution: tighten the waist and abdominal muscles throughout the process, straighten your back and slow down the movement.

16264.name: Bent-over Dumbbell Tricep Extension
16264.description: stand naturally, bend your knees slightly, try to bend over until your back is parallel to the ground, and tighten your waist and abdominal muscles. hold the dumbbells with both hands, and clamp the big arms against both sides of the body. straighten your arms, pause briefly and bend your elbows until your small arms are perpendicular to the ground.
16264.breathing: exhale when you straighten your arm and inhale when you bend your elbow and put down the dumbbell.
16264.key_points:
keep your lower back tense throughout the movement.
when you straighten your arm, you will feel a distinct contraction on the back of your big arm; you may feel a slight burning sensation after many times.
16264.mistakes:
mistake: arch your back, and swing your big arms up and down.
solution: reduce the bending range, keep the whole back straight; clamp your big arms simultaneously, keep them close to the sides of the body throughout.
16264.notes:
bend down, tighten your waist and abdominal muscles, and keep your back straight.
straighten your elbows and clamp the body with big arms.
bend your knees.

16270.name: Nod And Raise Head
16270.description: sit on the chair, put your hands on the thighs naturally, keep the waist and back straight, and keep your back close to the chair. put your hands behind the cervical spine to ensure the neck is fixed throughout the movement. when nodding your head, keep your lower jaw close to your neck, and when raising your head, raise your lower jaw upward.
16270.key_points:
when nodding your head, the muscles at the back of the neck feel slightly pulled.
when raising your head, the front muscles of the neck feel slightly pulled.
after the movement, there is a sense of stretching in the neck.
16270.mistakes:
mistake: your neck swings back and forth, following your head nodding and raising.
solution: hold the back side of the cervical spine with your hand and slowly complete the movement while keeping the cervical spine still.
16270.notes:
keep your neck fixed throughout the whole movement.
keep your head down and chin close to the neck.

16276.name: Two-way Head Turn
16276.description: sit in a chair, put your hands naturally on your thighs, and keep your waist straight and your back close to the chair. turn your head to one side, stay for a while, then turn back, and then turn to the other side. try your best to look behind when you turn your head, which will increase the pulling sensation of the neck.

16276.notes: turn your head to one side and try to look behind your body.

16282.name: Shrug And Sink The Shoulders
16282.description: stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, keep your chest up, stomach in, and shoulders down, and put your arms naturally on both sides of the body. raise your shoulder blades to the maximum extent, with a slight pause; then sink your shoulder blades to the maximum extent, with a slight pause; repeat the process in turn.
16282.breathing: shrug your shoulders and breathe in; sink your shoulders and breathe out.
16282.key_points:
when lifting up, you can't see your neck.
when sinking, you should feel the neck slender.
16282.mistakes:
mistake: too fast
solution: pause slightly after each stage of the action.
16282.notes: keep your shoulders down to the lowest point.

16287.breathing: shrug your shoulders and breathe in; sink your shoulders and breathe out.
16287.key_points:
when lifting up, you can't see your neck.
when sinking, you should feel the neck slender.
16287.mistakes:
mistake: too fast
solution: pause slightly after each stage of the action.
16287.notes: keep your shoulders down to the lowest point.

16288.name: Four-way Nod Head
16288.description: sit on the chair, put your hands naturally on your thighs, and keep your waist straight and your back close to the chair. rotate your head forward, backward, leftward, and rightward in a particular order.
16288.key_points: the neck has an obvious sense of strength and stretch.
16288.mistakes:
mistake: the speed of movement is too fast.
solution: slow down the action, and feel the muscle's strength and contraction.
16288.notes: sink your shoulders throughout the movement, do not shrug, and pause for a while to feel the stretch in your neck when you finish each nod.

16294.name: Lying Alternate Upper-half Leg Raise
16294.description: keep your waist close to the ground, lift your hips off the ground, and there is a sense of tightness in the lower abdomen. put your hands on both sides of the hips, hook up your toes, and lift your legs when they drop to about 45°, and there should be no tension in your waist. keep the knee joints of both legs fixed, and there should be no kicking action.
16294.key_points: keep your whole abdominal muscle tight throughout, and the longer the action lasts, the stronger the burning sensation of the abdominal muscles.
16294.mistakes:
mistake: the waist can not be on the ground.
solution: do not drop your legs too low.
16294.notes:
keep your waist close to the ground.
keep your abdominal muscles tight.

16300.name: Half Roll Back
16300.description: sit on the yoga mat, keep your legs slightly bent and hip-width apart, and keep your back straight. when inhaling, extend your head and spine towards the ceiling. when exhaling, roll your tailbone toward the pubis, tighten the pelvic floor muscles, tilt the pelvis backward, and slowly flex the spine backward. make your spine form a "c" with a sense of extension. inhale and return to the starting position.
16300.breathing:
inhale through the nose.
exhale through the mouth.
16300.key_points: tighten your pelvic floor muscles and abdominal muscles.
16300.mistakes:
mistake: your waist bulges back excessively.
solution: lean back your pelvis slightly and drive your spine as a whole to extend backward.
16300.notes:
exhale, roll the tailbone toward the pubis, tilt the pelvis backward and tighten the abdominal muscles.
keep your spine extended.
